introduction: Our clothes, plastic buckets, water pipes, and vehicle tires—these are all 'Polymers'. A polymer is a large macromolecule formed by the repeated linking of many smaller units called 'Monomers'.

core_concepts.title: Natural vs. Synthetic Polymers
core_concepts.description:
1. Natural: Cotton (Cellulose), Wool, Silk, and Natural Rubber. 
2. Synthetic: Nylon (The first fully synthetic fiber), Polyester, Polythene, and Bakelite.

core_concepts.title: Types of Plastics
core_concepts.description:
1. Thermoplastics: These plastics get softened or 'melt' on heating and can be easily remolded into new shapes. (e.g., Polythene, PVC - used for making pipes). 
2. Thermosetting Plastics: Once molded into a shape, they 'cannot be softened or melted' again by heating. They are extremely rigid. (e.g., Bakelite, Melamine).

core_concepts.title: Rubber and Vulcanization
core_concepts.description:
Natural rubber is a polymer of 'Isoprene'. In its raw form, it is very soft, sticky, and not very useful. 
Vulcanization: To make rubber hard, strong, and highly elastic, it is heated with 'Sulfur'. This process is called Vulcanization (discovered by Charles Goodyear).

core_concepts.title: Teflon
core_concepts.description: It is a special polymer (Polytetrafluoroethylene) on which oil and water do not stick. It is heavily used for coating 'Non-stick cookware' (pans).

important_entities.name: Rayon
important_entities.significance: Rayon is widely known as 'Artificial Silk'. It is a semi-synthetic fiber because it is made by the chemical treatment of a natural raw material—'Wood Pulp' (Cellulose).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: What are electrical switches made of?
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Students often just tick 'plastic'. Remember, electrical switches and the handles of pressure cookers are made of 'Bakelite' (a thermosetting plastic) because it is an excellent 'Bad Conductor' of both heat and electricity, and it won't melt.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Thermo-'setting' means its shape is permanently set. It will not melt again. Thermoplastics are 'plastic' (flexible/moldable).

exam_strategy_tips: SSC's most favorite question: 'Which polymer is used for the non-stick coating on utensils?' Answer: Teflon.
